newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major-no shifts in EU policy before election.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major-no shifts in EU policy before election.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday there would be no change in his government's policies concerning the European Union before the election.
"There is not going to be any further shifts in policy," Major said on Sky Television. In the same interview, he said UK elections would not be held later than May 1.

The government has stated that it will keep its options open on whether it would join a single European currency. Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday he thought it was unlikely European economic and monetary union would go ahead on schedule, on January 1, 1999.
But many Conservative MPs are pushing for the prime minister to rule out British participation in European economic and monetary union. Some wish to withdraw from the EU altogether.
"I believe there is no doubt we continue in the EU. About half our trade goes to Europe, huge numbers of our jobs depend on Europe," Major said.

But he said he continued to guard against moves towards European federalism. "What we have to do is to make sure that we don't get dragged in a direction that is not in the British interest. That is the fear people have, that we will get dragged down...a federalist route."
